messages.subject: How to profile a model to determine it's "category"?
messages.subject_clean: How to profile a model to determine it's "category"?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm working to try and find out if a model some researchers I work with can be optimized. Having read through several issues on the adcomp tracker I located this comment

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/122#issuecomment-159552952

Notably on page 16 there is a table explaining how models are processing time in AD, outside AD (Cholesky factorization/Inverse subset)  in R GC/other.

Does anyone know how to begin to determine these numbers for a model? TMB::benchmark seems to provide details on Cholesky factorization and how parallelization affects it but is there some other utility I cannot find that provides the time spent in the various parts of the algorithm?

Thank you very much,

Mike

messages.body_plain:
Profiling from R may give you some useful information:

Rprof(); obj$fn(); Rprof(NULL)
summaryRprof()

Rprof(); obj$gr(); Rprof(NULL)
summaryRprof()

Look for 'updateCholesky' and 'solveSubset'...

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: retape error
messages.body_plain:
For anyone else: I most frequently encounter this error when I have listed a parameter in MakeADFun that is not used within the C++ code.

On Tuesday, February 28, 2017 at 9:44:33 PM UTC Kasper Kristensen wrote:
> Seems you have encountered an unfortunate name collision. There's an integer variable 'index' declared in the objective_function class. That's why you didn't get a compilation error. Your program was actually using this internal index variable which led to the strange 'TMB_epsilon' error.
>
> From: tmb-...@googlegroups.com [tmb-...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of jefflaake [jeff...@gmail.com]
> Sent: Tuesday, February 28, 2017 9:52 PM
> To: TMB Users
> Subject: [TMB users] Re: retape error
>
> Never mind.  I fell back to old-fashion debug approach of throwing out code and found the offending piece of code. Nothing to do with data and parameters. I was using an int variable index that was not declared in the code.  I had moved this code into the objective function from a separate function and in doing so forgot to copy over the declaration for index.  I thought this should have been a compile time error but apparently not. I'm "learning" more c++ one mistake at a time. I'm not certain why it ran for any model but it did.
>
> --jeff
>
> On Tuesday, February 28, 2017 at 12:15:47 PM UTC-8, jefflaake wrote:
> > Can anyone give me guidance on what to look for with regards to the following error from MakeADFun
> >
> > Error in retape() :
> >   Error when reading the variable: 'TMB_epsilon_'. Please check data and parameters.
> > In addition: Warning message:
> > In retape() : Expected object. Got NULL.
> >
> >
> > It says to check data and parameters but I don't have a variable TMB_epsilon_ so not sure what to look for.  With different models, MakeADFun does run successfully. The model changes the design matrices describing the model which are part of the input data. I looked at the data list and parameter list passed to MakeADFun but there is nothing that stands out as being different and it all looked fine. Is it because there is a disagreement of types? I searched for parts of this error on the wiki and internet but came up empty. I also debugged into MakeADFun and retape but ran into the generic error message in which TMB_epsilon was a value of a variable in the message but it didn't help me work out the problem.
> >
> > I realize this may not give enough info to work out what is wrong but any direction would be appreciated.
> >
> > regards --jeff
>

messages.subject: Convergence criteria
messages.body_plain:
I have what is probably an ill-determined random effects model which does not always converge. I have a two part question.
How can I relax the convergence criteria (in nlminb)?

The error message when the minimizer gives up is a bit spartan:
Error in newton(par = c(logbeta = -7.44239271957212, logbeta = -7.43808037040032,  :
  Newton failed to find minimum.
So, is it possible get a "snapshot" of the parameter and random effects estimates when the minimizer gives up?

Thanks,
John

messages.subject: Re: Convergence criteria
messages.body_plain:
Hi John, nlminb has a control argument which has tolerance specifications. I'd also try setting trace=1 to see console updates of fixed effects. I think if you pull out obj$env$last.par it will give you the last parameter vector evaluated (fixed and random effects). You could rebuild the obj without random effects and put that back through to get the joint likelihood and maybe something obvious would pop out? I assume that message means the inner optimizer failed. Lastly, I'd run the model through tmbstan  <https://github.com/kaskr/tmbstan>to see if full MCMC integration helps diagnose issues. -Cole
